prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance–Outbound Load Control Desk eligibility/closeout handoff; excludes aircraft loading. Custody controlled throughout; monitored areas, task-assigned access only.
Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies operating-departure identity/timing/routing/destination and Flight Cutoff Advisory to Baggage Control System (Velvet), authoritative identity/flight/screening/status record; validates assignments/cutoffs/allowances, records releases/alarms/dispositions/checks, presents routes, authorizes original-path returns. Revised assignments need approval; holds/missed cutoffs prohibit release.
Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit stages without reassociation; sends Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk. Bag Tag Printer produces unique durable tags/Calibration Witness Tag; replacements authorized. Transfer Bag Feeder meters checked arrivals; sends Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station: verifies identity/location/matches, flags discrepancies, sends Bag Match Query.
Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) controls lanes/induction; produces Recovery Route Card. Induction Tray Conveyor meters/scans/spaces readable-identity, valid-route bags; interlocks stop feed; unexpected stops prevent entry/clear approach. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel) captures tags/images; South Gate Scanner produces Manual Rescan Receipt; both require healthy status. Operator/Image Resolution Desk records dispositions; inconclusive images require physical inspection/identity agreement; unresolved/mismatched bags held. Faults hold feed pending disposition.
Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) preserves identity, routes cleared bags, diverts unresolved bags; sends Chute Occupancy Note. Secondary Inspection Chute excludes unrelated bags. Security Duty Manager resolves holds/access, verifies seals/escalates discrepancies using Explosives Response Team’s Custody Seal Log; team assesses events, communicates approved-channel dispositions. Return requires identity/outcome/authorization agreement. Pebble (full name unspecified) secures response area/directs handling.
East Make-Up Conveyor: guards/capacity; West Make-Up Conveyor: allocation metering. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) receives Airline Ramp Coordinator’s Carousel Release Slip; requires sequence/clearance/window/capacity, valid screening/destination.
Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern): occupancy, holds/stops/recovery/approvals, exception ownership. Maintenance Technician: isolation, inspection/accounting, fault reporting, calibration; consults recovery card. Restart: personnel clear, guards restored, alarms understood, route available. Preserve safe routes; bypasses require approved maintenance.

New part:
S218: The Bag Reconciliation Station compares scanned bag identities against the expected flight population and flags missing or duplicate records for resolution.
S219: The Airline Ramp Coordinator uses the Bag Match Query to review unresolved bag-to-flight mismatches before loading authorization is granted.
S220: The East Make-Up Conveyor moves reconciled bags toward the correct flight position without bypassing required identity checks.
S221: The West Make-Up Conveyor remains subject to the same controlled access and reconciliation rules as other make-up equipment.
S222: The Transfer Bag Feeder accepts transfer bags only when their identity and intended onward flight can be verified.
S223: The Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the flight assignment, reconciled bag count, and operational status are consistent before accepting the loading record.
S224: Before aircraft loading, the Airline Ramp Coordinator verifies that the bag identity is readable, the flight assignment is current, and the security disposition permits loading.
S225: The physical bags presented for loading must agree with the reconciled records, and every unexplained count or identity difference blocks acceptance.
S226: A bag is ready for departure only after screening release, custody continuity, final reconciliation, and loading checks are all complete and recorded.
S227: Operational monitoring provides a continuous view of baggage throughput, equipment availability, queue growth, screening status, and reconciliation exceptions.
S228: The Baggage Control System records bag events and reports missing, duplicate, or delayed event sequences for operational review.
S229: The Concourse Zone Controller reports equipment state changes and alarm conditions to the operations monitoring function.
S230: The Induction Tray Conveyor is monitored for stops, accumulation, and sustained operation below its approved rate.
S231: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter is monitored for availability, recirculation, fault frequency, and output rate against the approved operating plan.
S232: North Gate Scanner performance is assessed using availability, image capture quality, alarm frequency, and screening completion records.
S233: South Gate Scanner performance is assessed using the same approved service measures and screening completion criteria.
S234: The Image Resolution Desk reports unresolved images, review backlog, and processing time against the locally approved service target.
S235: The Bag Reconciliation Station reports unmatched records and count differences, which remain subject to resolution before acceptance.
S236: The Flight Data Gateway is monitored for message timeliness, completeness, and interface errors affecting flight assignment data.
S237: The Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit is monitored for service availability, transaction completion, and accumulation at its entry point.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
